coverage_notes: Exhaustive sweep across information foraging theory foundational literature, contemporary peer-reviewed research, and applied HCI/visualization work. Coverage includes: (1) seminal works by Pirolli & Card (1995-2007) establishing IFT as cognitive-ecological framework; (2) core concepts: information scent, patch models, diet optimization drawn from optimal foraging theory in behavioral ecology; (3) canonical HCI and information visualization authors (Shneiderman, Norman, Tufte, Munzner) providing interface design principles underlying why poor cues drive information seeking failures; (4) foundational decision theory (Simon's bounded rationality/satisficing) explaining why users "good enough" through interfaces; (5) related information behavior models (Bates' berrypicking); (6) contemporary peer-reviewed empirical studies (CHI 2024-2025, arXiv 2024-2026) examining how IFT adapts to LLM-based chatbot environments and user flight from traditional search to conversational interfaces; (7) modern applications in RAG optimization, graph-based search, conversational search systems; (8) practitioner synthesis sources bridging theory to web design (NN/G, IxDF). Deduplication excluded duplicate arXiv/ResearchGate mirror URLs, retaining primary canonical locations. Tier assignment: T2 for textbooks/canonical authors (Shneiderman, Norman, Tufte, Munzner, Simon), T1 for peer-reviewed conference papers (CHI, UIST, TOCHI, Psychological Review, IEEE) and open-access scholarly papers (arXiv, DTIC), T3 for practitioner essays/blogs (NN/G, IxDF). License notes assigned: redistribute-ok for arXiv papers and open-access sources; reference-only for proprietary publishers (Oxford UP, ACM paywalled), commercial sources (Nielsen Norman Group), and paywalled journals. Total ~35 sources providing comprehensive coverage of theory foundations, mechanisms, contemporary adaptations, and applied design implications across database visualization and RAG/conversational search contexts.

sources.title: Information Foraging
sources.notes: Seminal theoretical paper establishing information foraging theory framework, patch/diet models, cost-benefit optimization principles. Foundation for understanding how users adaptively navigate information environments via scent-based satisficing.

sources.title: Using information scent to model user information needs and actions and the Web
sources.notes: First published information foraging paper (SIGCHI 1995) introducing information scent concept as perceptual cues guiding navigation. Applies optimal foraging theory to web navigation behavior.

sources.title: Information Foraging Theory: Adaptive Interaction with Information
sources.notes: Comprehensive monograph synthesizing IFT framework, empirical validation, and applications to interface design. Canonical reference on how humans adapt to information environments under cognitive/temporal constraints.

sources.title: SNIF-ACT: A Model of Information Foraging on the World Wide Web
sources.notes: Computational implementation of IFT using spreading activation mechanism to calculate information scent. Validated model predicting link selection and patch departure behavior based on information scent thresholds.

sources.title: SNIF-ACT: A Cognitive Model of User Navigation on the World Wide Web
sources.notes: TOCHI publication detailing Bayesian satisficing model and Monte Carlo validation. Demonstrates SNIF-ACT 2.0 better predicts human navigation than positional models.

sources.title: Revisiting Human Information Foraging: Adaptations for LLM-based Chatbots
sources.notes: Contemporary arXiv paper (June 2024) applying IFT to LLM-based chatbot environments. Identifies key differences from patchy web: single non-patchy evolving patch, conversational interaction, contextual memory. Directly relevant to MetroGraph wedge on flight from UI to chat.

sources.title: Scent of Knowledge: Optimizing Search-Enhanced Reasoning with Information Foraging
sources.notes: 2025 arXiv paper directly connecting IFT information scent concept to RAG optimization. Models how LLM intermediate reasoning steps evolve information scent assessments during retrieval-augmented search.

sources.title: Bates' Berrypicking Model (1989, 2002, 2005)
sources.notes: Foundational information seeking model (Bates 1989) framing search as dynamic bit-at-a-time retrieval with evolving information needs. Complements IFT patch model; emphasizes interactive query refinement and browsing.

sources.title: Generative Echo Chamber? Effect of LLM-Powered Search Systems on Diverse Information Seeking
sources.notes: CHI 2024 peer-reviewed study comparing LLM-powered conversational search to traditional search. Demonstrates higher confirmatory behavior and opinion polarization—illustrates IFT failure modes when conversational interface lacks diverse information scent cues.

sources.title: Effects of LLM-based Search on Decision Making: Speed, Accuracy, and Overreliance
sources.notes: CHI 2025 empirical study on LLM-based vs. traditional search. Examines task speed vs. accuracy tradeoffs and hallucination effects. Relevant to understanding why users abandon traditional UIs for chat interfaces and resulting HCI failures.

sources.title: A New Era of Online Search? A Large-Scale Study of User Behavior and Personal Preferences during Practical Search Tasks with Generative AI versus Traditional Search Engines
sources.notes: Large-scale CHI study examining user behavior differences between generative AI chatbots and search engines. Documents user preference patterns and task completion differences relevant to IFT adaptation in conversational contexts.

sources.title: Understanding Mental Models of Generative Conversational Search and The Effect of Interface Transparency
sources.notes: arXiv paper examining mental models users construct for conversational search interfaces. Explores interface transparency effects on information seeking behavior and trust—critical for designing conversational interfaces with better scent cues.

sources.title: How does AI chat change search behaviors?
sources.notes: arXiv empirical study on behavioral shifts from traditional to AI chat search. Examines query patterns, interaction styles, and information evaluation strategies—directly relevant to understanding user flight from traditional UIs.

sources.title: Conversational Search -- A Report from Dagstuhl Seminar 19461
sources.notes: Comprehensive survey report on conversational search as emerging paradigm. Covers interaction models, evaluation challenges, and design considerations distinct from traditional search—foundational for understanding conversational interfaces as alternative to graph-based UI.

sources.title: Information Farming: From Berry Picking to Berry Growing
sources.notes: 2026 arXiv paper extending berrypicking and foraging metaphors. Proposes 'information farming' as active information environment construction—relevant to understanding how conversational systems actively generate content vs. traditional navigation of fixed information patches.

sources.title: Neural Approaches to Conversational Information Retrieval
sources.notes: arXiv survey on neural methods for conversational IR. Covers multi-turn interactions, context modeling, and information seeking patterns in dialogue systems—provides technical context for LLM-based interface design.

sources.title: Designing the User Interface: Strategies for Effective Human-Computer Interaction
sources.notes: Canonical HCI textbook (Shneiderman & Plaisant, 6th ed.). Foundational work on direct manipulation, visualization principles ('overview first, then details'), task taxonomy—establishes design principles that improve information scent and reduce cognitive load compared to poor UIs.

sources.title: The purpose of visualization is insight, not pictures: An interview with Ben Shneiderman
sources.notes: ACM Interactions interview with Shneiderman on visualization design. Articulates principles of visual encoding that support information discovery—directly relevant to database visualization in MetroGraph.

sources.title: The Design of Everyday Things: Key Principles
sources.notes: Summary of Norman's foundational work on affordances, signifiers, mental models, gulf of execution/evaluation. Establishes psychological principles explaining why poor interface cues (weak information scent) create user frustration and flight to alternatives.

sources.title: Envisioning Information
sources.notes: Canonical work on information visualization and data presentation. Establishes principles for effective visual encoding, layering, color use—foundational for designing database visualization interfaces that support information foraging.

sources.title: The Visual Display of Quantitative Information
sources.notes: Tufte's foundational work on statistical graphics, data-ink ratio, and visual design principles. Establishes standards for minimizing cognitive load and maximizing information density—critical for high-scent interface design.

sources.title: Visualization Analysis and Design
sources.notes: Munzner's comprehensive framework for visualization design (nested model: characterize task/data → abstract → encode/interact → execute). Provides systematic approach to designing graph/database visualizations that effectively support information foraging tasks.

sources.title: Ambient Findability
sources.notes: Morville's work on findability in information architecture. Connects to IFT by emphasizing metadata, navigation cues, and search integration as determinants of user success in locating information—foundational concept for high-scent interface design.

sources.title: Bounded Rationality (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
sources.notes: Foundational work on Simon's bounded rationality and satisficing decision-making. Provides cognitive/economic basis for IFT cost-benefit models: users satisfice (seek 'good enough') rather than optimize due to cognitive/temporal constraints.

sources.title: Graph Visualization and Navigation in Information Visualization: A Survey
sources.notes: IEEE survey on graph visualization techniques and navigation strategies. Directly applicable to metro-map-style graph visualization design; covers node-link layout, interaction patterns, and information scent in graph navigation.

sources.title: Graph drawing and information visualization
sources.notes: ACM Computing Surveys paper on graph drawing algorithms and visualization. Covers layout, edge routing, and visual encoding for graph-based information systems—foundational for MetroGraph's database visualization approach.

sources.title: A critical analysis of cognitive load measurement methods for evaluating the usability of different types of interfaces
sources.notes: arXiv paper analyzing cognitive load in interface design. Connects interface complexity to user performance and mental effort—explains why surface-area-bloated RAG/workflow-graph tools fail (excessive cognitive load vs. conversational chat).

sources.title: Minimize Cognitive Load to Maximize Usability
sources.notes: NN/G practitioner guide on cognitive load principles. Summarizes how interface design affects working memory, attention, and task performance—applied perspective on why poor-scent interfaces drive user abandonment.

sources.title: Nielsen's Heuristics: 10 Usability Principles To Improve UI Design
sources.notes: Practical synthesis of Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics. Evaluates interface quality on visibility, user control, error prevention—framework for assessing why interfaces fail at information scent communication.

sources.title: Interactive Query Clarification and Refinement via User Simulation
sources.notes: arXiv on interactive query refinement. Relevant to understanding how users dynamically adapt queries in conversational systems vs. traditional search—connects to berrypicking and evolving information needs in IFT.

sources.title: A Survey of Conversational Search
sources.notes: Comprehensive 2024 arXiv survey of conversational search systems. Covers interaction paradigms, evaluation, user studies—provides landscape of LLM-based search alternatives to traditional UI, relevant to understanding user flight from graph/workflow tools.

sources.title: Integrating Knowledge Graphs and Visualization Dashboards for Advance Data Discovery in VESA
sources.notes: arXiv paper on knowledge graph visualization for data discovery. Combines semantic web with visual analytics—directly relevant to designing database visualization interfaces that support information foraging.

sources.title: S-Paths: Set-Based Visual Exploration of Linked Data Driven by Semantic Paths
sources.notes: Semantic Web Journal paper on visual exploration of linked data using semantic paths. Provides patterns for navigating graph-structured data that support information discovery—applicable to MetroGraph's graph visualization approach.

sources.title: Patchy Perception: Rethinking Eye Movements through the Lens of Foraging Theory
sources.notes: 2025 bioRxiv paper reframing visual attention as foraging behavior. Demonstrates users spend more time on information-rich stimuli and optimize travel time to high-value targets—validates optimal foraging principles apply to visual information seeking.

sources.title: Cognitive maps, cognitive collages, and spatial mental models
sources.notes: Tversky's foundational work on spatial cognition and mental representations. Explains how people construct and navigate spatial/conceptual models—foundational for understanding how graph/metro-map visualizations support or hinder information navigation.

sources.title: Direct Manipulation Interfaces
sources.notes: Seminal HCI paper on direct manipulation principle (continuous object representation, rapid feedback, reversibility). Establishes design approach that improves information scent and reduces gulf between user intent and interface capabilities.

sources.title: Information Foraging: A Theory of How People Navigate on the Web
sources.notes: Nielsen Norman Group practitioner article synthesizing IFT for web design. Explains information scent, enrichments, cost-benefit calculations—applied perspective bridging theory to design practice for web interfaces.

sources.title: Information Foraging Theory | The Glossary of Human Computer Interaction
sources.notes: IxDF glossary entry synthesizing IFT concepts and applications. Covers patches, scents, diet model—practical reference for understanding IFT terminology and application to interface design.

sources.title: User Interaction Design Patterns for Information Retrieval Systems
sources.notes: Paper documenting design patterns for information retrieval UIs. Covers search, browse, faceted navigation, results presentation—patterns that enhance information scent and support diverse information seeking strategies.

sources.title: An Optimal Foraging Approach to Information Seeking and Use
sources.notes: Foundational application of optimal foraging theory to information seeking (Library Quarterly 1987). Establishes formal framework connecting biological foraging to information behavior—theoretical foundation for IFT.

sources.title: Conversational UI and AI Agents: Why the Hybrid Trap Kills Adoption
sources.notes: Practitioner essay on conversational UI design failures. Documents how poorly-integrated chat/UI hybrids create cognitive friction and user abandonment—directly relevant to MetroGraph's wedge on 'worst of both worlds' in agent-builder UIs.

sources.title: How should my chatbot interact? A survey on human-chatbot interaction design
sources.notes: 2019 arXiv survey on chatbot interaction design patterns. Reviews conversation models, turn-taking, feedback—provides design context for understanding conversational interfaces vs. traditional UI.
